transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-12
Time: 09:30 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (PM), Arjun (Eng Mgr), Lena (SWE), Ethan (SRE), Priya (Product Eng)

Summary/Notes: quick internal roadmap + launch readiness check; include incident review from last week staging outage, make sure runbooks, canary and rollback are solid.

[00:00] Maya: okay good morning everyone um thanks for joining on short notice, we'll try keep this tight 45 to 60 minutes, agenda is roadmap status, launch checklist, and that staging incident postmortem quick review.
[00:18] Arjun: yeah thanks, quick context, we pushed the release candidate into staging on monday and had that kv-cache warmup regression which caused request timeouts under the continuous batching path.
[00:35] Lena: yes, the cold-start path didn't populate prefix cache as expected, so the first few requests hit a slower kernel path, and that compounded with batching window being high.
[00:50] Ethan: SRE perspective, we saw 500s for about 12 minutes, autoscaler kicked, but the canary didn't failover cleanly because rollback policy wasn't triggered on that metric.
[01:05] Priya: ok, so first thing is are the runbooks up to date? who owns the rollback playbook?
[01:20] Lena: I updated the runbook last sprint but I think the automated rollback triggers are still in Ethan's queue, we had a TODO on threshold tuning.
[01:35] Ethan: yep, that's mine, I was planning a follow-up to tune the 95th p99 thresholds and wire the alert to the canary controller. I haven't pushed the playbook link to the on-call page yet.
[01:50] Maya: action: Ethan, please finalize canary config and rollback playbook, share by next friday. we'll record that as a must-have for launch.
[02:03] Arjun: regarding roadmap, we wanted the advanced batch optimizer in for cost targets, but given this incident and time constraints, i propose we cut that from the initial rollout and put it in the next milestone. that reduces surface area.
[02:20] Priya: agree, less risk at launch. can we instead focus on better QA coverage for the existing batching paths and prefix caching?
[02:30] Lena: yes i can add e2e tests that simulate cold-prefix traffic and validate performance. i need about a week to get reliable metrics.
[02:45] Maya: great. also we need to confirm docs: ops runbook, SLOs, and the support escalation matrix are in the shared drive. who will own the final signoff?
[03:00] Priya: I'll own signoff for ops docs, and Maya will do cross-org signoff with PM and support.
[03:12] Ethan: small note, the staging incident was partly because we were testing a low-latency kernel selector change; do we have a way to replay that traffic or reproduce reliably?
[03:25] Lena: i reproduced locally with smaller seq lengths but the composite failure required the batching window plus the new kernel path. i'll add the repro script to the tests.
[03:40] Arjun: backlog trimming: i'll remove the batch optimizer and deprioritize telemetry changes that are not blocking launch. we should keep the quantization improvements in the next sprint.
[03:55] Maya: timeline: launch target window is end of May, ideally 2025-05-27 for the initial hosted rollout. if next-week items slip we should push.
[04:10] Priya: we need compliance checkbox: SOC 2 items around audit logs and encryption at rest; are these done for the launch?
[04:22] Ethan: ENCRYPTION: kms integration is in place for dedicated/private but for hosted API we need to validate key rotation docs and retention policies, i'm 80% done.
[04:35] Maya: ok add Priya as owner for audit confirmation; include any remaining items in the checklist.
[04:45] Arjun: on testing, can we run a pre-launch smoke test that includes canary traffic with synthetic latency spikes?
[04:58] Lena: yes, i'll add scenarios: cold-starts, kv-cache misses, and kernel selector path variations.
[05:12] Ethan: oncall readiness: we'll need an escalation path, pager rotations, and a war room link; i can create the war-room doc and calendar invites.
[05:25] Maya: perfect.
[05:30] (brief cross talk)
[05:40] Priya: incident postmortem quick notes: root cause was kernel selector + batching window + cache warmup, mitigation was to revert the kernel change and increase batching window thresholds. long term we need better unit tests around kernel selection heuristics.
[05:58] Arjun: and we should add perf assertions into CI so regressions fail faster.
[06:12] Maya: let's recap next steps: arjun trims scope, lena adds e2e tests and repro scripts, ethan finalizes canary/rollback and war-room, priya audits SOC2 checklist, and maya will send out the updated checklist and coordinate signoffs.
[06:30] Maya: anything else?
[06:36] Lena: one more small ask— docs for model catalog version pinning should be clearer for customers of Dedicated; i'll make a doc and share.
[06:48] Maya: noted. thanks everyone, i'll follow up with a quick summary email and updated checklist. meeting adjourned.

References/links mentioned (to be shared in follow-up):
- Launch checklist doc (internal link)
- Runbook: /docs/oncall/kv-cache-rollbacks.md (to be updated)
- Canary config draft (link to repo PR #412)
- E2E test harness and repro script (link to test repo)

End of transcript.
